name: LM2596
description: Classic 40 V, 3 A, 150 kHz non-synchronous buck in TO-263: robust and forgiving, but big and inefficient next to modern synchronous parts.
notes: Needs a 3 A Schottky diode and a large inductor (typ. 33 µH) plus bulk electrolytics.
ON/OFF pin is active-low: tie to GND for always-on.
5 mA quiescent current: poor for battery standby.

en.note: ~ON/OFF (pin 5) is active low: below ~1.3 V = regulator ON, above 1.3 V (up to 25 V max) = OFF (VIH/VIL 1.3 V typ at 25 C; ON guaranteed below 0.6 V, OFF above 2 V over temperature). Pin table: if shutdown is not needed, wire it to GND or leave it open; either way the regulator runs. Figures 9-10/9-13 tie it to GND, so tie to GND. The 25 V limit comes from the pin table and sec. 8.3.1/8.3.2 (the abs-max table has no ON/OFF row). Delayed start / UVLO circuits in sec. 8.3.1-8.3.2 (add 47 kΩ ON/OFF-GND if the Zener is > 25 V).

notes: Non-synchronous voltage-mode buck, internally compensated, fixed 150 kHz (127-173 kHz at 25 C, 110-173 over temp); frequency drops in second-stage current limit. VREF 1.23 V (1.193-1.267 at 25 C). Peak switch current limit 4.5 A typ (3.6-6.9 at 25 C). VSAT 1.16 V typ at 3 A. Max duty 100 %, no min on-time spec.

Inductor: µse the nomographs. Fixed versions: Fig 9-5/9-6/9-7 (max VIN vs load). ADJ: compute E*T [V*us] = (VIN - VOUT - VSAT)*(VOUT + VD)/(VIN - VSAT + VD)*1000/150 kHz with VSAT 1.16 V, VD 0.5 V (Eq. 8), then read Fig 9-8 at the max load. Fig 9-8 at 3 A (read off the graph): E*T ~13-20 -> 22 µH (L41), ~20-30 -> 33 µH (L40), ~30-44 -> 47 µH (L39), ~44-60 -> 68 µH (L44). Datasheet example: 28 V -> 20 V, 3 A, E*T 34.2 -> 47 µH (L39).

Common cases at 3 A: 12 V -> 5 V = 33 µH (L40), the datasheet's own example (Fig 9-6, Table 9-3 'VIN <= 15 V' row). 24 V -> 5 V = 47 µH (L39) from Table 9-3 ('VIN <= 40 V'). On Fig 9-6, 24 V sits just under the L39/L40 border at about 25 V (33 µH), and the ADJ E*T of 28 V*us also reads 33 µH, so 47 µH is the table's conservative pick. 12 V -> 3.3 V = 22 µH (L41): on Fig 9-5 the 33/22 µH border at 3 A is about 15 V, and the ADJ E*T of 16.8 V*us also gives 22 µH; Table 9-3 only has 10 V (22 µH) and 40 V (33 µH) rows. 24 V -> 3.3 V = 33 µH (L40). 24 V -> 12 V = 68 µH (L44) per Table 9-3 ('VIN <= 30 V'). At 2 A: 24 V -> 5 V = 68 µH (L38).

Ripple ratio implied by the nomograph (Fig 9-4): dIL is about 20-30 % of max load for 2-3 A designs, rising to 30-50 % at 0.5 A (kInd above = the 2-3 A band). Inductor current rating per Table 9-1 codes (L39-L41 = 3.5 A, L44 = 3.4 A, L38 = 3.1 A).

Output cap: low-ESR switching-grade aluminium electrolytic 82-820 µF (or solid tantalum 10-470 µF). Do not exceed 820 µF. Voltage rating >= 1.5x VOUT, often higher to get low ESR (a 16-25 V cap roughly halves the ripple of a 10 V one). ESR has both an upper limit (ripple) and a lower limit (too-low ESR, e.g. all-ceramic, can make the loop oscillate). Typical circuits: 220 µF 25 V (fixed) / 220 µF 35 V (ADJ) Nichicon PL; Table 9-3 gives 330 µF/35 V for 5 V at 3 A, VIN <= 15 V. Electrolytics are not recommended below -25 C (use tantalum). For ripple < ~15-20 mV add a post LC filter (1-5 µH + low-ESR cap).

Feed-forward cap (ADJ only): CFF across R2, required for VOUT > ~10 V and also µsed with very-low-ESR COUT (e.g. tantalum). Typically 100 pF to 33 nF; Eq. 10: CFF = 1/(31e3 * R2). Table 9-6 values by VOUT (through-hole electrolytic column): 2 V 33 nF, 4 V 10 nF, 6 V 3.3 nF, 9 V 1.5 nF, 12 V 1 nF, 15 V 680 pF, 24 V 560 pF, 28 V 390 pF (SMD tantalum column: 220 pF at 24-28 V). Use ceramic (not Z5U), film or silver mica. Eq. 10 and the table disagree: for the 20 V example (R2 15.4 k) the equation gives ~2.1 nF but the text picks 560 pF. Prefer Table 9-6.
R1 recommended 1 kΩ 1 % (range 240 Ω-1.5 kΩ) between FEEDBACK and GND; R2 = R1*(VOUT/VREF - 1). Example: 20 V -> R2 = 15.4 k.

Input cap: low-ESR aluminium electrolytic (or surge-tested tantalum) from VIN to GND, close to the IC. Size it by RMS ripple current >= 1/2 the DC load current (50 % at 40 C ambient, 75 % at 70 C), voltage >= 1.25x (sec. 9.1.1) to 1.5x max VIN for electrolytics, 2x for tantalum. Typical circuits µse 470 µF 50 V; the design examples pick 680 µF 35 V (12 V in) and 680 µF 50 V (28 V in). Be careful with high-K ceramic input caps: severe ringing at VIN. No separate small HF cap in the typical app.

Layout: heavy-line loops (CIN, diode, GND, COUT) short and wide, ground plane or single-point ground; keep the OUTPUT (switch) node copper small; FB divider near the IC; prefer closed-core (toroid/E-core) inductors, since open-core flux near FB/COUT causes ripple or instability.

Catalog check: VIN 4.5-40 V, ADJ VOUT 1.2-37 V, 3 A, 150 kHz, async all agree with the datasheet. The TI product page lists VOUT min 3.3 V (family-level), which does not apply to the ADJ part. The abs-max table oddly lists SD/SS, delay and flag pins (likely left over from a sister part); VIN abs max is 45 V.
The TO-263 tab is GND: solder it to at least 0.4 in² of copper (2 in² of 2 oz copper for full current).
